title: Every owner uses on
summary: Possession uses on with every owner, even when several people own the thing.
objectives: Use on with every possessor, including several owners.
Recognise the pattern, then produce it with the supporting words shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Possession uses on with every owner, even when several people own the thing.
Minulla on pallo means “I have a ball”; meillä on pallo means “We have a ball”. Do not choose olemme or ovat because the owners are plural. Those forms belong to sentences such as “We are …”.
keyPoints: Use one singular thing and the owner form shown by the prompt.

steps: minulla means “I as the owner”.
Use fixed on for possession with minulla; olen belongs to an “I am” sentence.
kirja (“book”) stays in its basic singular form: one thing.
sinulla means “you as the owner” for one person.
Sinulla still takes on, not olet: this pattern says what someone has.
koira (“dog”) stays in its basic singular form: one thing.
hänellä means “he as the owner” or “she as the owner”; this example uses “she”.
Hänellä on means “she has” or “he has”; the gender choice does not change on.
auto (“car”) stays in its basic singular form: one thing.
meillä means “we as the owner”.
Meillä names several owners, but the possession verb stays on, not olemme.
pallo (“ball”) stays in its basic singular form: one thing.
teillä means “you as the owner” for a group.
Teillä addresses a group here; use on, not olette.
kynä (“pen”) stays in its basic singular form: one thing.
heillä means “they as the owner”.
Heillä names several owners; use on, not ovat.
peli (“game”) stays in its basic singular form: one thing.
sinulla means “you as the owner” for one person.
Changing the thing to a cat leaves the same sinulla on pattern.
kissa (“cat”) stays in its basic singular form: one thing.
heillä means “they as the owner”.
A front-vowel noun such as tyyny changes neither the owners nor fixed on.
tyyny (“pillow”) stays in its basic singular form: one thing.

commonMistakes: Possession uses on with every owner: meillä on, not meillä olemme; heillä on, not heillä ovat.
Several owners can have one thing. A plural owner does not turn pallo into a plural noun.

Olla means “to be”; possession uses its fixed on form with every owner, including we and they.

answerDiagnostics.category: Fixed on in possession: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The -lla/-llä phrase is the possessor. In this possession pattern the verb stays fixed, so do not conjugate it to match the owner.
